result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_radius()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get graph radius (minimum eccentricity). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28786-L28860){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_radius(unconnected=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Radius](/assets/graphs/get-radius.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with each node's eccentricity in a badge. The center nodes C and D, drawn in the accent color, reach every other node within 2 hops, so the radius is 2." width="100%"} The radius is the minimum of all node eccentricities. Nodes with eccentricity equal to the radius form the center of the graph. A node's *eccentricity* is the distance to the farthest node it can reach. It is computed with a breadth-first search from every node, so distances are counted in hops (edge weights are ignored) and, in directed graphs, paths must follow edge directions. The radius tells you how close the best-placed node is to everyone else, which is useful for: - choosing where to put a facility, server, or coordinator so that the worst-case distance to anyone is as small as possible - comparing it with the diameter: a radius close to half the diameter indicates a compact, well-centered network, while a radius close to the diameter indicates one without a clear center - bounding the number of rounds a broadcast from the best starting node needs Because each node's eccentricity only covers the nodes it can reach, nodes that reach nothing have eccentricity `0`: an isolated node, or a node with no outgoing edges in a directed graph, makes the radius `0` under the default `unconnected=True`. `get_min_eccentricity()` is an alias of this method and `get_diameter()` is its counterpart (the largest eccentricity). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [unconnected]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls what happens when some nodes cannot reach each other. If `True` (default), each node's eccentricity only considers the nodes it can reach and the smallest one is returned, pooled across all components (so an isolated node yields `0`). If `False`, the method returns `None` for a graph that is not connected. For directed graphs this check uses weak connectivity (edge directions ignored). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum eccentricity, or `None` if disconnected (when `unconnected=False`). Also `None` for an empty graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star, the hub reaches every other node in one hop, so the radius is `1`: ::: {#8f6eb720 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C")]) ) graph.get_radius() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: In a path of five nodes, the middle node is at most two hops from either end, so the radius is `2`, half the diameter of `4`: ::: {#61a638a9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) (path.get_radius(), path.get_diameter()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (2, 4) ``` ::: ::: Adding an isolated node drops the radius to `0`, since that node reaches nothing. Use `unconnected=False` to get `None` instead of a misleading value for a disconnected graph: ::: {#ba250f05 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_node(label="loner") (graph.get_radius(), graph.get_radius(unconnected=False)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (0, None) ``` ::: :::
